name: What if the garage slab is cracked or uneven?

mainEntity.name: Can a garage still be converted if the concrete slab has cracks, slope, or settlement?
mainEntity.text: Can a garage still be converted if the concrete slab has cracks, slope, or settlement?

acceptedAnswer.text: A cracked or uneven slab does not automatically disqualify a garage conversion, but it can change the scope significantly. Hairline cracks are common and may be addressed during prep and finishing. Larger cracks, visible settlement, water intrusion, or slab movement are more serious because they can affect flooring, wall alignment, drainage, and the long-term performance of the living space. In some cases, the slab can be repaired and leveled. In others, part or all of it may need replacement or structural reinforcement. This is especially important if you plan to add a bathroom, kitchen plumbing, or heavier finish materials. In Los Angeles-area conversions, moisture control matters because garages are often below the standard comfort level of the main house. Before committing to a design, have the slab checked for slope, elevation changes, and signs of past water entry. If the floor is too uneven, the finished ceiling height may also be affected because floor buildup can reduce usable headroom. A good contractor will evaluate whether the slab can be salvaged or whether the repair costs make another layout more practical.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, but slab defects may trigger repair, leveling, waterproofing, or replacement depending on severity. Small cosmetic cracks are common, but major settlement, moisture intrusion, or uneven floors can affect finish quality, code compliance, and long-term durability, so the slab should be inspected before plans are finalized.
